string-array.name: about_changelog
string-array.item: 1.4.19|Incognito mode no longer crash-loops on Android 10 (the WebView data directory is secured before anything can load the provider — the crash that kept bouncing you to the normal tabs menu is cured, and the exit button now actually leaves incognito instead of landing you back on the incognito home); a page that fails to load no longer corrupts the tab address into an unfixable error URL — the error is an overlay with a Retry button, the tab keeps its real address, and intent:// links with no app installed load the site\'s web fallback (Facebook links work without the app); dragging a tab onto a group no longer leaves a hole in a long switcher grid (the change animation that kept the gap alive is bypassed for the drop); forced dark mode keeps thin lines, dividers and hamburger icons visible (light hairline colors are remapped so they don\'t invert into near-black); AI screen translate handles dense screens (the reply token cap doubles with an automatic retry when the answer hits the limit); Bing image search results now run under the real bing.com origin so the page\'s scripts, cookies and results actually load; the omnibox engine chip shows the active search engine\'s logo (Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, Brave, Startpage) and updates when you switch; every icon-only button carries a long-press tooltip; saved passwords can be added and edited by hand in the vault; and Bolt AI accepts temporary image and text attachments (never saved, cleared on close).

1.4.18|Dragging a tab onto a group card no longer leaves a hole in the switcher (the drag door now gets the same no-void reload the menu door got, plus a posted relayout that beats the settle-animation race, and ungrouping rides it too); the omnibox action row (copy, paste, duplicate, image search, voice) is visible the moment you tap the search box instead of appearing only after the first keystroke, and Copy on an empty field copies the current page address; dark mode inverts light pages at first paint instead of waiting ~3 seconds for sites that merely declare dark support (a site that darkens itself later is still pulled back), and background tabs get the same dark treatment; image search now carries your browser cookies and exact user agent through the upload and back into the results page (the grey broken-image report — the upload session and the results page are one session now), and Bing results saved as local pages load their images; AI translate with a custom model keeps the full fallback chain, retries and falls back on provider errors (the model that actually answers is named in a toast when it is not your pick); an external search (home-screen widget, selection toolbar, share sheet) now follows your last session — browsing incognito means the search opens in incognito instead of bouncing you back to the normal tabs menu.

1.4.17|Moving a tab into a group no longer leaves a void in the switcher grid (the grid layout manager span cache is invalidated on every move-to-group); the group sheet highlights the tab you are currently reading (accent rim + accent title) and every accent rim now draws 2dp inside its card edge so it never covers thumbnails or buttons; image search uploads at JPEG quality 90 with bilinear scaling (the grey-image report); dark mode no longer flashes white while a page loads — the inversion decision runs at first paint instead of after the page finishes loading, and the blank loading canvas is dark for sites under the dark engine; AI translate errors now leave the raw provider response in logcat under the AiBridge tag (the evidence for any future provider error); the core UI icons are Google Material Symbols Rounded at a consistent 24dp with theme-aware tinting; selecting text anywhere and choosing Search in Bolt (Incognito) runs the search in the private incognito process instead of bouncing you to normal mode.

1.4.16|Downloads are reliable again: a failed save no longer leaves a 0KB file behind (which used to force the next attempt into "name (1)" duplicates), blob: downloads route through the page-side JS bridge instead of dying in the network stack, and a file whose real type was learned from the server or its magic bytes always gets that type\'s extension (no more .bin); the tab switcher\'s drag never rebuilds the grid mid-gesture (the ghost-tab-on-move corpse — external changes now land when the drag ends); the group sheet\'s rows are full-width so the 3-dot menu docks at the edge instead of the middle; incognito mode is set before anything loads in the incognito process (a class-loading race could boot it in normal mode); the folder row of the tab you are reading lights up with the same accent rim and strip as loose tabs; the omnibox is two rows — the URL field keeps its full width (engine chip + clear only) and Copy / Paste / Duplicate / Image / Voice actions live on a strip below that appears while you type; switching tabs closes a find-in-page bar that used to bleed onto the next page; the omnibox dialog and the speed-dial drag ghost are cleaned up when the app pauses or dies.

1.4.15|The Downloads screen now hears the download engine directly (events instead of a 500 ms poll — progress updates land the instant a download advances, so switching screens never looks reset or stale); the tab switcher re-highlights the CURRENT tab on every reopen (a notification or external link that moved your reading tab used to leave the old one outlined); typing in the address bar is smoother twice over — the icon strip only re-lays-out when the empty/typing state actually flips, and the bookmark/history suggestion walk moved off the main thread so every keystroke renders instantly; two lingering handler leaks (the speed-dial hold timer and the omnibox suggestion debounce) are cleaned up when the browser is destroyed.

1.4.14|Tab groups open a bottom sheet whose rows you can now long-press and DRAG to reorder (the Move up/Move down buttons are gone); a "Search in Bolt" from another app\'s text selection opens in a NEW tab instead of overwriting the page you were reading; the address bar hides the camera/paste icons the moment you type, giving the URL the full field width (clear + mic only, Chrome-style); bookmarks, history and saved pages opened from the incognito side return to the incognito browser instead of leaking into the normal one; picking a 12 MP photo for visual search no longer risks an out-of-memory crash (bounds-first decode to a 1280 px cap with an OOM retry ladder); Bookmarks and History gain a search bar that filters by title or URL as you type.

1.4.13|The text-selection toolbar now shows a proper "Search in Bolt" label (the PROCESS_TEXT filter carries its own label plus the text/plain MIME on every launcher face); the address bar asks your search engine for completions only after a 300 ms typing pause — one request per pause, never per keystroke, never in incognito, with an off switch in Settings; the favicon cache is capped at 1000 icons / 50 MB and evicts least-recently-used files (reads refresh the use stamp); a spare WebView is pre-warmed in the background at app start, so opening a new tab no longer pays the ~300 ms construction stutter; interrupted downloads resume from the exact byte they stopped at — now with an ETag/If-Range check so a file that changed server-side restarts cleanly instead of splicing two different files into one corrupt download.

1.4.12|AI screen translation uploads drop from 2–4 MB to ~200 KB (1280 px / 75% quality — no more mobile-network timeouts or 400/413 rejections); tab groups open a vertically scrollable bottom sheet instead of the squished inline strip, and the switcher scrolls to your active tab even when it lives inside a folder; the incognito tabs view finally runs in incognito mode (a missing process flag made it list and open NORMAL tabs); Bolt joins the text-selection toolbar and the system "Web search" surface; the omnibox gains an engine-switch chip beside the field and a camera/image-search icon that routes a photo to the selected engine\'s visual search.

1.4.11|Screen translation no longer leaks the whole screen on rotation (the headless OCR WebView now lives on the app context instead of pinning the closed screen forever); every remaining tab-list walk in the browser and switcher UIs holds the list lock, killing the remaining crash-on-rotate/switch races; the adblock engine reads the request\'s Accept header, so extension-less tracker scripts are finally typed — and blocked — as scripts; the per-site wipe retries a briefly-locked cookie jar instead of silently skipping it.

1.4.10|The adblock engine stops compiling ~130,000 regex Patterns (a ~130 MB memory corpse — plain-literal rules now ride one compact Aho-Corasick scan per request, identical blocking at a fraction of the RAM); a dead write-only WebView registry that pinned every closed tab\'s context in memory is deleted, so closed tabs finally free their memory; the tab list no longer races the background media service (the ConcurrentModificationException corpse); the release signing key\'s password was rotated after exposure in private history — same certificate, updates still install in place.

1.4.9|Dropping a tab group beside another group lands exactly beside it (the invisible \"teleport to the bottom\" corpse: a stale position memory sent drops to the wrong end of the list, and the settle wrote the wrong side); the top-right menu is grouped into labelled sections; every tab inside a tab group and every shortcut inside a home folder gets its own visible \"\u22ef\" menu — edit name and link, de-group, delete — no hold gesture needed.

1.4.8|Empty tab groups settle exactly where you leave them (a neighbour-anchored position memory replaces the shifting row index) and tabs can finally sit right beside an empty group; the shortcut flow asks for the folder only after you choose Add to browser home; folders grow from their own window and edit sheet (a + tile and an Add shortcut row); site settings are chunked into labelled groups.

1.4.7|Only the tab group you actually hold moves (empty groups stop travelling with their neighbours — and drag themselves at last); background playback survives rotating the phone to landscape; the add-shortcut dialog can file a site straight into a home folder.

1.4.6|The home folder window\'s icons finally drag (a listener-eating corpse under every gate); empty tab groups keep their top spot when switching to follow-tab-order; every delete in the app — tab, shortcut, folder, bookmark, saved page, watch-later — gets a 3.5-second Undo.

1.4.5|Switching groups-on-top to follow-tab-order keeps the layout exactly where it was (then drag anything anywhere); the in-folder tab drag and the folder-window icon drag actually work on device (a scroll-stealing corpse); tabs and folders no longer vanish on the switch (atomic saves, no stale cross-process rewrites, duplicate-folder heal).

1.4.4|The hidden game paces itself (floatier jumps, slower bars, wider gaps); tabs rearrange freely beside folders in follow-order and inside the folder rows; folder-window icons rearrange by dragging; saved passwords fill every account of a site (with a picker) and two-step sign-ins remember the username.

1.4.3|The hidden game survives a failure (tap to retry works); switching group placements never moves your folders; password saving actually writes the vault (and autofill finally has something to fill).

1.4.2|The hidden game actually launches (a spawn-loop hang froze it on a black screen); empty folders no longer vanish in follow-tab-order; About lives in deep settings; bookmarks and shortcuts can rank above history while typing.
1.4.1|The folder window lays its icons out as a proper matrix; About gains this changelog and a hidden game; one tab order across both group placements.
1.4.0|The launcher folder window, the draggable tab groups, the disappearing-folder fix and this About screen with the update checker.
1.3.100|The grouping dwell takes a full second to fill; sign-in-with-GitHub round-trips ride one stable identity (the qwen connect fix).
1.3.99|The version agreement: the UA and the client-hints claim the same Chrome version (the grok gate).
1.3.98|The home drag vs. page-swipe clash fixed; the desktop site survives back-navigation.
1.3.97|No more phantom home refresh on early drags; the icon menu is quicker and fully iconified.
1.3.96|The home-drag crash fixed; save-AI-response and the whole-page PDF work.
1.3.95|The new-tab crash fixed; the search-history fill button; the unhurried home menu.
1.3.94|The home-screen crash loop fixed; the honest backup import; the ask-first dark pipeline.

Live sync between Bolt and Google Authenticator is not possible — Google keeps that data locked to its own app (end-to-end encrypted, no API). QR transfer is the sanctioned way in both directions:

● Google Authenticator → Bolt: in the Google app open the ⋮ menu → Transfer accounts → Export accounts, screenshot the QR code, then here: + → Import from Google Authenticator and pick the screenshot. With more than 10 accounts Google shows several QR codes — import each one.

● Bolt → Google Authenticator: long-press an account here → Show QR code, then in the Google app tap + → Scan a QR code.
